review_type: Independent visual review of all nine supplied Chromium screenshots
scale: 0–10; evaluated within the intended low-resolution, low-polygon asset style
verdict: The apartment, shared corridor and close surrounding buildings communicate the brief convincingly. The principal remaining visual blocker is exterior containment: recognizable interior-looking picture frames and unexplained thin projections are visible on the apartment building exterior. Most occupied-room views are stronger than the building-context view.

read: all nine round-02 PNG screenshots using view_image
scope.callers_tests_fixtures_config_exports: Not affected by this report-only change

strengths: Furnished, compact kitchen/dining layout retains a coherent lived-in asset-pack aesthetic.
Fridge front and side form solid opaque yellow surfaces; the nearby terracotta pot reads as a closed opaque volume.
Plant leaves preserve shaped edges and visible surface patterns rather than becoming rectangular cards.
A close neighboring facade is visible through the distant bedroom window.
issues: Cabinet fronts are quite dark, but their forms remain readable; this is a minor lighting preference rather than a required correction.

strengths: Visible entrance wall has an opaque door and continuous wall, with no window on this shown section.
The full terracotta pot and broad leaves look opaque; the leaf silhouettes remain intact.
TV, small table and bookcase provide plausible domestic scale.
Doors on both sides, repeated ceiling lights and the far landing make this read clearly as a shared apartment corridor.
Narrow proportions and subdued lighting support the intended oppressive setting.
Rough, visibly pixelated wall/floor/ceiling textures are consistent with the requested restored treatment and should be retained.
issues: The far stair connection is difficult to read in this distant angle, but the dedicated landing capture supplies the missing context.

strengths: The opposite brick facade almost entirely fills the window, successfully conveying close urban spacing.
Both visible AC units sit on solid masonry between window openings with visible support brackets.
No AC/window intersection is visible here; the domestic foreground ties the exterior to the occupied room.
The adjacent building blocks the outward view across nearly the whole window, delivering the claustrophobic bedroom setting.
AC units occupy clear wall spaces between neighboring windows.
Bed, curtain panels and window frame retain the established low-poly visual language.
issues: Very repetitive facade/window treatment is visible, but it is acceptable for this style and does not require extra decoration.

strengths: The apartment belongs to a substantial multi-storey block with roofline, street entrance and adjacent buildings.
The narrow side passage establishes real exterior separation rather than a flat backdrop.
issues: Several recognizable framed pictures are visible on the exterior courtyard-facing wall around x655–775, y415–500. They resemble the indoor wall pictures in 03-east-window.png, and break the building-envelope illusion.

Thin horizontal projections cross or extend from two upper street-facing windows around x1070, y237 and x1060, y385. Their attachment and purpose are not legible, so these read as stray geometry or interior fittings protruding outdoors.
The street and pale sidewalk end against a flat gray background on the right. This exposes the set boundary in this diagnostic camera, though the room views do not establish that players can see it.

strengths: The opposing balconies feel close enough to compromise privacy.
Balcony slabs meet the wall beneath door openings, with front/side mesh rails and visible support brackets.
The AC unit is placed between windows with no visible overlap.
The window frame and curtains anchor the view inside the apartment.
Tall surrounding facades and the narrow ground passage create convincing urban enclosure.
Bins, rubbish and modest graffiti give the service court a plausible use without overwhelming the scene.
Visible balcony brackets and AC supports connect the added fittings to masonry; no clear window intersection is visible in this angle.
issues: The bright narrow opening at the far left of the end building suggests the finite backdrop from this diagnostic angle; assess it only if a player can access this view.

strengths: A turning stair, handrail and stacked windows establish a vertical circulation core beyond the corridor.
Its rough materials match the deliberately retained corridor treatment.
issues: The close upper flight/soffit dominates the top half and overlaps the top of the visible far window in projection. This makes the stair arrangement harder to understand from this particular camera; the image alone cannot establish a structural or clearance error.
The near landing and rail continuation are cropped, so safe traversal and complete rail connections cannot be verified visually.

prioritized_issues.classification: Visual sign-off blocker for the complete building exterior
prioritized_issues.title: Contain room props within the exterior building envelope
evidence: 05-building-context.png: framed images around x655–775, y415–500 on the courtyard-facing exterior.
05-building-context.png: unexplained narrow projections around x1070,y237 and x1060,y385 on the upper street-facing windows.
prioritized_issues.confidence: High that the exterior artifacts are visible; their exact source and whether the thin bars are interior fittings cannot be established from screenshots alone.
prioritized_issues.minimal_correction: Check the identified frames and bars against the exterior wall planes. Move offending room props fully inside, or correct the local shell thickness/placement that exposes them; remove unintended protruding fittings. Preserve the room arrangement and existing materials. Re-capture the building-context angle and affected room window after the smallest correction.
prioritized_issues.avoid: Do not redesign all facades or add decorative exterior features to conceal accidental intersections.

prioritized_issues.classification: Conditional polish, not an established gameplay blocker
prioritized_issues.title: Do not expose the finite set from approved player cameras
evidence: 05-building-context.png: street/sidewalk meets flat gray beyond the right edge of the built environment.
07-court-detail.png: narrow bright opening at the far-left end of the court.
prioritized_issues.minimal_correction: Once player camera positions are approved, check whether these boundaries are visible. If they are, extend only the necessary background occluder. No environment expansion is justified solely for temporary review cameras.

brief_checks.furnished_interior_retained: Visually supported by 00, 01, 03 and 04; exact parity with the original asset is not independently checked.
brief_checks.apartment_in_wider_building: Supported by 02, 05 and 08, subject to the exterior containment defect in 05.
brief_checks.no_entrance_side_windows: No window is visible on the entrance wall section in 01. The images do not show every point of that entire building side.
brief_checks.corridor_and_other_flats: 02 shows a shared corridor with multiple apartment-style doors. Interiors of those other flats are not shown.
brief_checks.balcony_ac_attachment: The visible balconies and AC units have plausible wall attachment and avoid obvious window collisions in 03, 04, 06 and 07. Not a full geometry audit.
brief_checks.fridge_opacity: Visible pass in 00: no room geometry shows through its front or side.
brief_checks.pot_opacity: Visible pass for the full pots in 00 and 01: solid sides and top/soil surfaces.
brief_checks.leaf_opacity_and_silhouette: Visible pass in 00 and 01: leaves have distinct shaped edges with no obvious see-through leaf interiors or opaque rectangular alpha-card backgrounds.
brief_checks.rough_corridor_textures: Retain them. No texture cleanup requested or recommended.

limitations: All nine actual supplied PNGs were opened with view_image; no implementation claims or source code substituted for inspecting them.
No browser session was run, no implementation files edited, and no geometry/material source audit performed.
Screenshots cannot prove depth ordering while moving, collision/head clearance, interactions, other-flat contents, performance, or the absence of artifacts at unshown angles.
Review cameras are temporary; set-boundary and stair-composition observations do not justify changing approved player views without checking them.
No previous-round images or original asset pack were opened, so this report does not quantify visual improvement or exact retention.
skipped_and_risk: Skipped runtime/navigation and source-geometry checks. Exterior prop containment remains the concrete visual risk; screenshot-only passes apply only to the visible surfaces.
